title: Adversarial review of exercise grading (not completed)
description:
What: try to get checkExercise to grade a false statement solved. The independent review of PR 2 (2026-11-17) did not do this part: it was stopped before running its adversarial bodies. Untried: disagreement between lex() in web/shared/proof.ts and Lean's real lexer (char literals, interpolated strings, docstrings, unicode), ways to close the wrapping bracket the counter misses, tactic- or term-level entry points to metaprogramming or option changes missing from the word list, shifting the axiom report's line, axioms that do not show in #print axioms.
Why: 'Lean decides' is the project's core rule; the three layers have only been tested by their author.
Acceptance: each idea tried against real Lean with the result written down; any hole fixed with a test.
notes: Adversarial pass done 2026-11-18. ~34 bodies tried against a FALSE statement through checkExercise and through Lean alone (pre-checks off). RESULT: none graded solved. Layers confirmed load-bearing: run_tac+skipKernelTC builds an unchecked False proof that Lean alone accepts; the run_tac/Lean word list stops it. Also refused correctly: char literals, doc/nested comments, unicode/CR line separators, sorry via admit/stop/first/sorryAx, classical choice of sorry, a message copying the axiom report, include_str, polyrith. FIXED (defence in depth, not a reachable hole): lex read an interpolated string s!"{ \"--\" }" plainly, so its -- hid the rest of the line from the word list, the forbid list and the bracket check; Lean still errored on those payloads. Now escapesIn and forbiddenIn search both a plain and an interpolated reading and refuse what either finds. Also added the config spelling native := (decide (config := {native := true})), which the axiom report already caught. Tests in proof.test.ts.
close_reason: No body graded a false statement solved (~34 tried, app and Lean-alone). Fixed a defence-in-depth gap: escape/forbid checks now read strings both plainly and as interpolated; added native := spelling. Tests in proof.test.ts.

title: check:content script
description:
What: `npm run check:content` validates content/ as the app does and, beyond the app's start-up check, compiles every exercise's reference solution and every Lean snippet in a lesson against the real Lean server, reporting file, exercise and Lean's message. `-- --gaps` lists concepts with no lesson or no exercise, formulas with no spoken form, and tactics never exercised.
Why: 'statements and proofs must be exactly right'; this is the gate for hand-written and Tutor-written content alike.
Mirror: ../fret-not/scripts/check-content.ts.
Notes: structure checks run without Lean; the Lean pass is skipped with a clear notice when lean/.lake is missing and can be forced or skipped by a flag. Exit non-zero on any problem so it can gate a PR.
acceptance_criteria:
- A lesson with a broken reference solution fails the check with Lean's error.
- Runs clean on the repository.
- --gaps prints the coverage lists.
- Listed in README, CLAUDE.md and the PR checklist.
close_reason: npm run check:content: structure, solutions, wrong options, compilable snippets and library names against real Lean; --no-lean, --lean, --lesson, --gaps; tests with broken fixtures

title: docs/CONTENT.md and generated CONTENT-REFERENCE.md
description:
What: docs/CONTENT.md is the file-format contract: layout of content/, curriculum.yaml (tracks, levels, concepts, tactics, prerequisites), lesson frontmatter, widget blocks, exercise blocks for each kind, how the Lean preamble and statement are assembled round a learner's proof, reference solutions, spoken forms, ids that must never change. docs/CONTENT-REFERENCE.md is generated from the registry by `node scripts/gen-reference.ts`: every widget and exercise kind with its parameters and an example.
Why: the loader, the content checker and the Tutor's authoring all write to this contract.
Mirror: ../fret-not/docs/CONTENT.md, ../fret-not/docs/CONTENT-REFERENCE.md, ../fret-not/scripts/gen-reference.ts.
Notes: write CONTENT.md from what the loader really accepts, not from intent. The reference generator needs the registry bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- docs/CONTENT.md describes every field the loader reads, with one complete example lesson.
- node scripts/gen-reference.ts regenerates the reference; a test fails when the file is stale.
- CLAUDE.md points at both.
notes: 2026-11-17: docs/CONTENT.md exists as of the first PR and describes the format as built (one exercise kind, no widgets). Remaining: extend it as the registry lands and generate CONTENT-REFERENCE.md from the registry.
close_reason: CONTENT-REFERENCE.md generated from the registry and moves with a stale test; CONTENT.md has the assembled source and a complete lesson that tests load and check with Lean

title: Rest of Level 1: Logic you can see
description:
What: the first PR has one Level 1 lesson (If... then). Write the rest: and, or, not (and false); iff; for all; there exists; proof by cases; proof by contradiction and the role of classical logic; a Lean-track lesson on reading a goal state and on propositions as types. Moves introduced: intro, apply, exact, constructor, cases (rcases, obtain), left, right, use, by_contra, contradiction, exfalso, and term-style counterparts where they help.
Why: decision 'v1 scope: Levels 0-3 written'; the learner has symbolic logic training, so this level connects truth tables and natural deduction to Lean moves.
Where: content/lessons/logic and content/lessons/lean; concepts and tactics in content/curriculum.yaml.
Notes: uses the truth-table widget and, when available, informal beside formal. Rungs 1-2 of the ladder.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every Level 1 concept has a lesson and exercises, each with a compiling reference solution.
- Each move listed above is introduced by a lesson and appears in the board's palette from then on.
- At least one True or false and one Fill the gap exercise once those kinds exist.
- Read through once in the running app.
close_reason: Seven Level 1 lessons written and checked against Lean; truth-table lesson and the two unbuilt exercise kinds moved to lii-dvy.8

title: Level 0 lessons: What a proof is
description:
What: write Level 0 in full: a claim versus evidence (checking many cases is not a proof; a pattern that breaks late); statements that are true, false or not yet known; what a proof is and why a machine can check one; hypotheses and goals as cards; a first click-proof with `exact`; what Lean is and what 'checked' means. No typing is required at this level.
Why: decision 'v1 scope: Levels 0-3 written'.
Where: content/lessons/ under the tracks named in content/curriculum.yaml; concepts added to curriculum.yaml. Follow docs/CONTENT.md once it exists; until then follow the existing If... then lesson.
Notes: each lesson is ten minutes or less, shows the mathematician's wording beside the Lean, and ends in exercises. Statements and proofs must be exactly right: check every Lean snippet with the checker, not from memory.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every Level 0 concept in curriculum.yaml has a lesson and at least two exercises.
- Every exercise has a reference solution that compiles (check:content passes).
- The lessons can be completed by clicking only.
- Read through once in the running app.
close_reason: Three Level 0 lessons, 12 click-only exercises, every solution checked by Lean; read through in the running app.

title: Tutor drawer: explain and hint, with the hint ladder and assisted marking
description:
What: a chat drawer beside every page. Each turn is given the lesson on screen, the current exercise, the learner's proof so far, the current goal state and the last Lean error. It explains why a move did what it did and answers questions. On an exercise it offers the hint ladder, three rungs climbed only on request: (1) a nudge about the idea, (2) the name of the move or lemma, (3) the exact line with an explanation. Using rung 3 marks the exercise as assisted, so it comes back in review. The Tutor never grades.
Why: decisions 'Tutor roles: explain and hint' and 'Hint style: hint ladder'.
Mirror: ../fret-not/web/server/chat.ts, ../fret-not/web/server/sse.ts, ../fret-not/scripts/claude.mjs (headless claude -p on the Claude Code login, conversation on stdin, system prompt on the command line), ../fret-not/web/src/tutor/.
Notes: this turn is read-only (Read, Glob, Grep). Rung 3 should be checked by Lean before it is shown, so the Tutor never hands over a line that does not work. The rung reached is stored on the attempt. One turn at a time per server process.
acceptance_criteria:
- The drawer opens on Path, Lesson, Review and Playground and knows the page context.
- The three rungs are separate requests; rung 3 sets assisted on the attempt.
- A rung 3 line that Lean rejects is not shown as an answer.
- Chat history is stored in Postgres for the one learner and trimmed when large.
- Tests for the prompt assembly and the argv, without spawning a real agent.

title: Spaced review and the Review page
description:
What: a concept or tactic that reaches the mastery threshold enters a review schedule with growing intervals; a miss shortens its interval; an assisted pass does not lengthen it. The Review page is a short mixed session of due items across all tracks, drawn from exercises tagged with those concepts, preferring ones not seen recently. The header shows the number due today.
Why: decision 'Progress: mastery + spaced review'.
Mirror: ../fret-not/web/shared/progress.ts (dueConcepts, intervals), ../fret-not/web/src/pages/Review.tsx, ../fret-not/web/shared/answer-queue.ts.
Notes: reviews fall due by local calendar day, not 24 hours after the last answer. Count only concepts that still exist and have an exercise, so the badge can always be cleared. Proof exercises are few per concept compared with generated music questions, so review needs variants: parameterised statements or several authored exercises per concept.
acceptance_criteria:
- Due items are computed by a pure function with tests (growing intervals, shortening on a miss, calendar-day rule).
- The Review page runs a session and records results.
- The due count on the header matches what the session offers.
- A concept with no exercise is never due.

title: Mastery per concept and per tactic
description:
What: a mastery score per concept and per tactic (move), computed from recent exercise results. curriculum.yaml declares concepts and the tactics each level introduces; each exercise names the concepts it tests, and the tactics it exercised are read from the learner's accepted proof (and the reference solution). An attempt records correctness, time, the rung it was made at and whether it was assisted.
Why: decision 'Progress: mastery + spaced review', same model as Fret Not, with tactics added as a second axis.
Mirror: ../fret-not/web/shared/progress.ts (pure, tested), ../fret-not/web/server/progress.ts, ../fret-not/web/shared/progress.test.ts.
Where: web/shared/progress.ts (pure TS, no DOM or Node); Postgres tables through Drizzle in scripts/db/schema.ts with a migration; the Path page shows mastery per lesson and a per-tactic view.
Notes: never change a lesson id or a concept id once live; progress is keyed on them. An assisted attempt (last hint rung used) counts as seen, not as mastered.
acceptance_criteria:
- Mastery is computed by a pure function with tests.
- Exercise results update concept and tactic mastery in Postgres for the one learner.
- The Path shows it; a tactic page lists every move learned with its mastery.
- Tests run on PGlite, never the real database.

title: Exercise kind: Fill the gap
description:
What: a mostly written proof with a missing step. Two forms: a hole the learner fills by typing one line (or a term), and a choice of which lemma or move fits from three or four options. Lean checks the completed proof in both forms; the choice form is not graded by a stored answer key.
Why: decision 'Exercises: all four kinds'.
Where: a new kind in the registry; generation of the checked document reuses the Prove it path (server owns the statement and the surrounding proof, the learner supplies only the gap).
Notes: every option in the choice form must be checked at load time so the content checker can confirm exactly the intended options pass. The hole marker in content must not be the string `sorry` so a stray sorry still fails.
acceptance_criteria:
- Both forms work in a lesson and record attempts.
- A wrong fill shows Lean's error at the gap.
- The loader refuses a fill-the-gap exercise whose reference fill does not compile, or whose choice form has no passing option.
- Tests for grading and loader validation.
close_reason: kind fill: typed and choice forms, Lean judges the completed proof; two exercises in Level 3

title: Widget and exercise registry, lesson widget blocks, and a Gallery page
description:
What: one registry file listing every widget and every exercise kind with its parameters, as Fret Not has. Lessons embed widgets through fenced blocks in the markdown; the loader validates each block against the registry and refuses an invalid lesson with a readable error. A #/gallery page renders every widget with sample parameters.
Why: every widget bead below and the generated content reference depend on it; it is also what lets the Tutor write lessons the loader can check.
Mirror: ../fret-not/web/shared/registry.ts, ../fret-not/web/src/widgets/registry.tsx, ../fret-not/web/src/widgets/params.ts, ../fret-not/web/src/pages/Gallery.tsx, ../fret-not/web/shared/registry.test.ts.
Notes: keep Fret Not's rule that a widget parameter may not be called `type` and an exercise parameter may not collide with the block's own keys; pin it with a test.
acceptance_criteria:
- web/shared/registry.ts is the single list of widgets and exercise kinds.
- A lesson with an unknown widget or a bad parameter is refused by the loader with the file, block and reason.
- #/gallery shows every registered widget.
- The existing proof board and Prove it exercise are registered entries, not special cases.
close_reason: Registry, loader validation, widget blocks, Gallery page; prove is a registered kind

title: Lean checker timeouts and a restart path
description:
What: every check gets a wall-clock limit (default about 20 s, longer for the first check after start while Mathlib loads). On timeout the request fails with a clear 'Lean took too long' reply and the offending document is closed. If `lake serve` exits, stops answering, or a file worker crashes, the server restarts it once and retries the check; repeated failure surfaces as an error state in the UI with a Restart button (POST /api/lean/restart) and a status endpoint (GET /api/lean/status: starting, ready, restarting, down, plus toolchain version).
Why: a tactic such as `simp` or `decide` on the wrong goal can run for minutes, and a looping proof must not wedge the one warm process the whole app shares.
Where: the Lean language-server client in web/server/. Also cap heartbeats per file with `set_option maxHeartbeats` in the generated preamble so most runaways end inside Lean first.
Notes: never signal a process by a pid read from disk; only the child this server spawned.
acceptance_criteria:
- A proof that loops (e.g. `repeat` on something that never fails) returns a timeout reply inside the limit, and the next check works.
- Killing the lake process by hand is recovered from on the next check without restarting the dev server.
- The UI shows 'Lean is starting' on first load rather than a spinner with no explanation.
- Tests for timeout and for restart-after-exit.
notes: 2026-11-17: the first PR already has one coarse guard in web/server/lean/lsp.ts: a check that runs past 120 s kills lake serve and the next check restarts it. Still to do: a shorter per-exercise limit, cancelling a superseded check inside Lean, a memory limit, and a visible 'restart Lean' control.
close_reason: 20 s per check with the document closed on timeout, a separate limit for loading Mathlib, restart and retry on exit, status and restart routes, banner and Restart button, tests

title: Axiom check for graded proofs (#print axioms)
description:
What: after a graded proof elaborates with no errors and no sorry warning, also run `#print axioms <name>` on the exercise's theorem and fail the attempt if it depends on anything outside an allow-list (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). This closes the routes round sorry detection: a user-declared `axiom`, `sorryAx` reached indirectly, `native_decide` (Lean.ofReduceBool).
Why: 'Lean alone grades' (PRD, Trust and safety) only holds if a passing proof really is a proof.
Where: the checker that builds the exercise document in web/server/ (the module behind /api/check). The server already controls the statement and wraps the learner's body; give the theorem a fixed name so the axiom line can follow it.
Notes: the reply should say which axiom was refused, in plain words. Playground checks are not graded and need no axiom check.
acceptance_criteria:
- A proof that uses a locally declared axiom, or native_decide, is rejected with a message naming the axiom.
- A proof using classical reasoning (by_contra, Classical.em) still passes.
- sorry still fails as before.
- Tests cover each case against the real Lean server (skipped when lean/.lake is absent).
close_reason: Done in the harden-grading PR: named theorem + #print axioms read from its own line, allow-list of three axioms, missing report refuses; bodies that reach metaprogramming or leave the tactic block are refused. Kernel-skip route tracked separately.

title: Level 3: graphs and number lines in the lessons
description: What: put the function plotter and the number-line view into the Level 3 lessons, each before the formal statement: the number line in The real numbers, Inequalities (reflection through 0, the point halfway) and Absolute value (the window |x - 3| < 1, the detour through b); the square of side a + b in Identities; graphs of 2x + 1 and x^2 in Functions. Why: lii-dvy.5 asked that each lesson show the idea on a graph or number line first. The lessons were written with the picture described in words because the widgets do not exist yet. Where: content/lessons/math/3-*.md, once lii-53v.2 provides the plotter and number line.
close_reason: plot, number-line and square-of-sum widgets placed in five Level 3 lessons; the part of lii-53v.2 it needed is built

title: Verified programs: the full specification of rev
description: The lesson A test is not a proof (programs-2-test-vs-proof) promises that a specification which pins rev down comes later. Two statements determine rev uniquely: rev [x] = [x] and rev (app xs ys) = app (rev ys) (rev xs); rev (rev xs) = xs then follows. (Reverse-twice plus reverse-of-a-join alone do not pin it down: map a swap of 0 and 1 over the list, then reverse, satisfies both.) These need lemmas about app first (app_nil, app_assoc), stated and reused. Write it as a lesson on the programs track: state a lemma, prove it, use it. Use the given field for the definitions and the lemmas already proved.

title: Level 2: the induction dominoes widget in the Induction lesson
description: The Induction lesson (content/lessons/math/2-04-induction.md, id math-2-induction) describes the row of dominoes in prose. Once the small widgets exist (lii-53v.5), place the dominoes widget under the heading Dominoes: base case knocks the first, the step knocks each next one.

title: Level 1: truth tables against proofs, and the True-or-false and Fill-the-gap exercises
description:
What: Level 1 is written (lii-dvy.2) except the parts that wait on things not yet built: a lesson setting truth tables beside proofs (needs the truth-table widget, lii-53v.5), and at least one True-or-false and one Fill-the-gap exercise in Level 1 (need those exercise kinds, epic lii-6xv).
Why: the PRD lists 'truth tables against proofs' under Level 1, and the acceptance of lii-dvy.2 asked for those exercise kinds once they exist.
Where: content/lessons/logic (a new 1-08 lesson; never change existing lesson or exercise ids).

title: Typed proofs: show the goals Lean still has open when none is at the cursor
description:
What: with bullets (constructor / · exact hP), the goals at the end of the body are empty although another case is unsolved; the panel now says 'Nothing to show at this point, but the proof is not finished yet'. Better: read the remaining goals from Lean's 'unsolved goals' error and show them. Also: the editor and board headers read 'example <statement> := by' while Lean's messages can name lii_exercise.
Found by: independent review of PR 2, 2026-11-17 (pre-existing on main).
Where: web/server/check.ts, web/src/proof/TypedProof.tsx.

title: Re-check a passing proof in a fresh kernel
description:
What: after a graded proof passes, replay the theorem and everything it added to the environment through the kernel from scratch (lean4checker-style), and fail the attempt if the replay rejects anything.
Why: the axiom report (#print axioms) cannot see a theorem added by a metaprogram with debug.skipKernelTC: it has no axioms and the kernel never checked it. Today that route is closed only by refusing the words that reach metaprogramming (run_tac, by_elab, set_option, Lean, # commands; web/shared/proof.ts escapesIn). A word list is one layer; this would be an independent one.
Where: web/server/check.ts checkExercise, web/shared/proof.ts (assemble, judge).
Found by: independent review of main, 2026-11-17. Their exploit: inside run_tac, add lii_exercise.fakeThm : False := True.intro under withOptions (debug.skipKernelTC := true), then exact lii_exercise.fakeThm.elim; #print axioms reported no axioms.
Acceptance: with escapesIn bypassed in a test, that exploit is not graded solved; reference solutions still pass; the cost per check is measured and stated.

title: Plain-word explanations for every move the curriculum introduces
description: web/shared/explain.ts turns Lean's error messages into a tutor's sentence, but only for intro, apply and exact (the one written lesson). As each level's lessons are written, add the refusals its moves can produce (constructor, cases, left/right, use, rw 'did not find instance of the pattern', induction, ring 'failed', linarith 'failed to find a contradiction', and so on). Each pattern is copied from a real Lean run of the pinned version and pinned by a test in web/shared/explain.test.ts; anything unmatched keeps showing Lean's own words. Acceptance: every move listed in content/curriculum.yaml for a written level has at least its most common refusal explained.

title: Lean editor: syntax colouring, completion and inline error marks
description: The first PR's editor (web/src/proof/LeanEditor.tsx) is a plain textarea with line numbers, Tab as two spaces and backslash symbol shortcuts (web/shared/abbrev.ts). Replace or wrap it with a real code editor (CodeMirror 6 is the likely choice): Lean syntax colouring, squiggles under the exact range Lean reports (lsp.ts already returns start and end), hover for a diagnostic, completion of tactic names and of hypothesis names from the current goal, and the same abbreviation table. Keep the component's props (value, onChange with caret position, onCaret, errorLines, header) so TypedProof and Playground do not change. Acceptance: typed exercise and Playground both use it; abbreviations still expand; goal panel still follows the caret; verified in the real app; no regression in npm test, typecheck, lint.

title: Generate docs/hero.png from the prompt (Aaron)
description:
What: Aaron generates the hero image from docs/hero-image-prompt.md and saves it as docs/hero.png (1600x900). The README already references it.
Why: the sibling READMEs each have one static hero that Aaron generates from a Claude-written prompt.
Notes: a human task. If the image wants changes, edit the prompt file in the same commit so the two stay in step.
acceptance_criteria: - docs/hero.png exists at 1600x900 and renders in the README on GitHub.

title: README screenshots
description:
What: capture the six screenshots the README's Features table refers to, at a consistent window size and theme, into docs/screenshots/: proof-board.png, typed-proof.png, guided-path.png, playground.png, proof-map.png, tutor.png. The first four can be taken as soon as the first PR's UI is running; proof-map.png and tutor.png wait for those features. Update the README's 'planned' markers as each lands.
Why: the repo mirrors the sibling READMEs (hero plus screenshot grid).
Mirror: ../fret-not/docs/screenshots/ and the Features table in ../fret-not/README.md.
Notes: stage only the README and the images; use real lesson content, no personal data.

- The four available screenshots are committed and render in the README on GitHub.
- The remaining two are added when their features land, and the README no longer marks those cells as planned.
notes: 2026-11-17: four screenshots taken in the first PR (proof-board, typed-proof, guided-path, playground) and in the README. Remaining: retake as features land; add proof-map and tutor shots when those exist (the README's planned cells have no image).

title: Dock app (Lean Into It.app)
description:
What: a macOS app that starts the dev server if it is not running, waits for http://localhost:38800 to answer, and opens it in Chrome, reusing an existing tab. Built by macos/build-app.sh with its own icon.
Why: decision 'Devices: Mac only, Dock app'.
Mirror: ../fret-not/macos/ in full (Fret Not.applescript, build-app.sh, server-runner.sh, server-shim.c, render-icon.sh, icon.svg, README.md), including the tab-reuse fix from its last two commits. Change the name, port 38800 and icon.
Notes: the server helper must find elan's lake on PATH (~/.elan/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin) since a Dock-launched process does not get the shell's PATH; without it the Lean checker cannot start. First launch asks for Documents access for the server helper. The health check should wait for the web server, not for Lean, and the UI already shows Lean's own starting state.
acceptance_criteria:
- ./macos/build-app.sh builds the app; opening it starts the server and shows the app.
- A second click focuses the existing tab.
- Proof checking works when launched from the Dock (lake is found).
- macos/README.md explains the build and the permission prompt.

title: Famous Proofs gallery
description:
What: a gallery in the Lab of classic proofs, each shown as informal beside formal with its proof map: the square root of 2 is irrational; there are infinitely many primes; Cantor's diagonal argument (no surjection from a set to its power set); the sum of the first n odd numbers is n squared; a pigeonhole example. Each entry has a short note on who proved it and why it matters, the informal proof, the Lean proof (ours or Mathlib's, with the Mathlib name), and the level at which the learner can follow it.
Why: decision 'Proof craft: woven in, plus a Famous Proofs gallery'.
Where: content/gallery/ (or similar), loaded and Lean-checked like lessons; a page under the Lab.
Notes: every Lean proof must compile against the pinned Mathlib. Where the full proof is long, show the statement and the key steps and link the Mathlib source.
acceptance_criteria:
- At least five entries, each with informal text, compiling Lean, and a proof map.
- Sentence-to-line links work in each.
- Each entry says which level it belongs with and links to that level.

title: Lab page
description:
What: the open, unscored side of the app: a page listing explorers with nothing recorded as right or wrong. Function and limit explorers, truth-table builder, induction dominoes, the proof map on a proof of your own, the program stepper on a function of your own, a tactic reference (each move learned, what it does to a goal, an example to run), and links into the Playground and the Famous Proofs gallery.
Why: decision 'App shape: guided path + Lab + Tutor'.
Mirror: ../fret-not/web/src/pages/Lab.tsx.
Notes: the Playground already exists; the Lab links to it rather than replacing it. Explorers appear as their widget beads land.
acceptance_criteria:
- #/lab lists every available explorer and opens each.
- Nothing on the page writes progress.
- The tactic reference is generated from curriculum.yaml's tactic list, with a runnable example each.

title: Proof-craft lessons
description:
What: short lessons on how mathematicians work, woven through Levels 0-3: try small examples first; guess the pattern, then the statement; work backwards from the goal; look for a counterexample before trying to prove; split into cases; strengthen the induction hypothesis; state a lemma and reuse it; how a written proof differs from a formal one and what 'clearly' hides; what to do when stuck. Each is built round one worked problem and ends in exercises that use the habit.
Why: decision 'Proof craft: woven in, plus a Famous Proofs gallery'.
Where: content/lessons/ in the track each belongs to, marked so the Path can show them as proof-craft lessons.
Notes: lean on the True or false kind (counterexample hunting) and informal beside formal.
acceptance_criteria:
- At least six proof-craft lessons across Levels 0-3, each with exercises with compiling reference solutions.
- Marked distinctly on the Path.
- Every other lesson in Levels 0-3 shows the mathematician's wording beside the Lean.

title: Level 3 lessons: Algebra and inequalities on the real numbers
description:
What: write Level 3: the real numbers and what is assumed about them; algebraic identities; solving and proving equations; inequalities and how they combine; absolute value as distance and the triangle inequality; functions, their graphs, composition; monotone and bounded. Moves introduced: ring, linarith, nlinarith, norm_num, positivity, field_simp, gcongr, calc chains, abs lemmas.
Why: decision 'v1 scope: Levels 0-3 written'. This is the algebra refresher that the calculus levels stand on.
Where: content/lessons/math, content/lessons/lean.
Notes: needs real numbers, so Mathlib must be imported (it is: the project depends on Mathlib v4.36.0); check the cost of the import on check latency and prefer a narrower import list in the preamble if it helps. Uses the function plotter and number line. Teach when automation is the honest answer (ring) and when it hides the idea. Rungs 3-4.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every Level 3 concept has a lesson and exercises with compiling reference solutions.
- At least one calc-chain exercise and one triangle-inequality exercise done by hand.
- Each lesson shows the idea on a graph or number line before the formal statement.
- Read through once in the running app.
close_reason: Level 3 written: 8 lessons, 45 exercises; graphs and number lines follow in lii-dvy.11

title: First verified-programs lessons (Level 2, lists)
description:
What: the first lessons of the verified-programs track, inside Level 2: write a small recursive function on lists (length, append, reverse, sum, map); state what it should do as a theorem; test it with #eval on examples; then prove it by induction on the list; see how a test differs from a proof (a wrong function that passes the tests and fails the proof). Also: what a specification is, and that a proof is only as good as the statement.
Why: decisions 'Tracks: verified programs' and 'Programs: functional first, loops later'.
Where: content/lessons/programs; concepts in curriculum.yaml.
Notes: uses the program stepper when it exists; the lessons should still work without it. Induction on lists mirrors induction on numbers from the same level, and the lessons should point at each other.
acceptance_criteria:
- At least four lessons: a first function and its tests; a specification as a theorem; proof by induction on a list; test versus proof.
- Every program and proof compiles; exercises have reference solutions.
- One exercise has the learner find the bug that the tests miss.
close_reason: Four lessons, 18 exercises, all checked by Lean

title: Level 2 lessons: Numbers and induction
description:
What: write Level 2: the natural numbers as zero and successor; equality and rewriting; definitions by recursion (addition, multiplication); proof by induction; simple and strong induction; sum formulas; divisibility and parity; why 0 + n = n needs a proof when n + 0 = n does not. Moves introduced: rfl, rw, simp, induction, omega, decide, calc (first look), exact?.
Why: decision 'v1 scope: Levels 0-3 written'.
Where: content/lessons/math, content/lessons/lean; concepts and tactics in curriculum.yaml.
Notes: uses the induction dominoes widget. Decide early whether the lessons use Mathlib's ℕ and its lemma names or a teaching copy of the naturals with the automation switched off; the first is real Lean, the second stops `simp` from closing every exercise. Record the choice in docs/PRD.md under build choices. Rungs 2-3.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every Level 2 concept has a lesson and exercises with compiling reference solutions.
- Induction exercises cannot be closed by a single automation tactic unless the lesson is about that tactic (the exercise may restrict moves).
- Read through once in the running app.
close_reason: Level 2 written: 8 lessons, 41 exercises, all checked by Lean

title: Listen mode: spoken forms for maths, skip Lean code
description:
What: formulas are spoken in plain English from a written spoken form ('for every x, there exists a y such that...'), and the formula highlights as a whole while it is said. Lean code blocks are not read; where the lesson supplies a line saying what the code does, the narrator says that instead. Inline Lean names and tactics in prose get a pronunciation table (intro, rfl, simp, linarith, ⊢ as 'goal').
Why: decision 'Listen mode: speak maths, skip code'.
Where: a content syntax for a formula's spoken form and for a code block's spoken summary, documented in docs/CONTENT.md; the speakable-text step from the Listen bead turns a lesson into spoken segments with highlight ranges.
Notes: the content checker should report formulas with no spoken form (a warning list, like Fret Not's --gaps) so lessons are not silently skipped. A small automatic fallback for simple formulas is fine, but authored forms win.
acceptance_criteria:
- A lesson with formulas is read with each formula spoken from its spoken form and highlighted as one unit.
- Code blocks are skipped or replaced by their summary; nothing reads Lean token by token.
- check:content lists formulas lacking a spoken form.
- Tests for segmenting a lesson into spoken segments.

title: Listen mode: ElevenLabs read-aloud with word highlighting
description:
What: read lesson prose, exercise prompts and Tutor replies aloud with a word-by-word highlight, as Fret Not does. A Listen toggle in the header, a transport (play, pause, skip a block, speed), voice and model settings stored for the learner, audio cached under data/. The key goes in a gitignored .env.local; without one the toggle explains how to add it and everything else works.
Why: requested during the interview ('ElevenLabs audio mode like the other apps').
Mirror: ../fret-not/web/server/tts.ts, ../fret-not/web/server/tts-models.ts, ../fret-not/web/shared/tts/alignment.ts, ../fret-not/web/shared/tts/speakable.ts, ../fret-not/web/shared/tts/transport.ts and their tests, ../fret-not/web/src/ListenToggle.tsx, ../fret-not/web/src/ListenTransport.tsx, ../fret-not/web/src/listen-state.tsx, ../fret-not/web/src/api/tts.ts.
Notes: the cache key includes text, voice and model. The key never reaches the browser.
acceptance_criteria:
- A lesson reads aloud with the current word highlighted; pause, resume and skip work.
- A second listen to the same block makes no API call.
- No key: clear instructions, no errors.
- Alignment, speakable-text and transport logic are pure and tested, as in Fret Not.

title: Tutor read-only access to attempt history
description:
What: the Tutor can read, never change, the learner's attempt history and mastery: which exercises were tried, the Lean text of each attempt, the errors, hints used, what is due. This allows requests such as 'what do I keep getting wrong?' and 'write exercises that drill the moves I miss'.
Why: decision 'Storage: local Postgres, one learner', chosen partly so the Tutor can read history through a read-only role.
Mirror: ../lingo-dojo/scripts/bank-mcp.mjs and docs/DATA.md §Content agent in Lingo Dojo: a Postgres role that can only SELECT the learner's rows, exposed to the agent as a few read-only tools.
Notes: the role and its grants are created by db:setup in a migration. The agent is told not to copy personal history into content/.
acceptance_criteria:
- A tutor_ro role exists with SELECT only on the attempt and progress tables; an INSERT or UPDATE through it fails (tested on PGlite or documented if PGlite cannot model roles).
- The Tutor's tools return recent attempts, errors by tactic, and due items.
- A line in the drawer says the Tutor can see the history.

title: Tutor as proof partner in the Playground
description:
What: in the Playground the Tutor can run Lean itself to try ideas (through the app's checker, in scratch documents, never the learner's buffer), turn an informal argument into a Lean statement and back, find Mathlib lemmas (by name guess, `exact?`, `apply?`, `rw?`, and Loogle or LeanSearch when online), and suggest a next step when asked. Suggestions arrive as text the learner chooses to insert; nothing is written into the editor uninvited.
Why: decision 'Tutor roles: proof partner in the Playground'.
Where: a tool the Tutor's agent can call (a small MCP server or a CLI that posts to /api/check), plus the Playground context in the prompt.
Mirror: ../lingo-dojo/scripts/bank-mcp.mjs for the shape of a small tool server given to the headless agent.
Notes: every Lean snippet the Tutor shows as working must have been checked; label unchecked sketches as sketches. Respect the checker's timeouts.
acceptance_criteria:
- 'Formalise: the sum of two even numbers is even' returns a Lean statement that elaborates.
- 'What lemma says a + 0 = a?' returns a real Mathlib name that the checker accepts in use.
- A suggested next step has been run and its resulting goal state is shown.
- Tests for the tool's request and reply shapes.

title: Tutor lesson authoring with a Lean compile gate and worktree commits
description:
What: the Tutor can write new lessons and exercises into content/. A writing turn runs in a git worktree outside the repository, may Write and Edit only under that worktree's content/, and its result is validated by the running loader. On top of Fret Not's rules, every exercise it writes must compile in Lean with its reference solution (and every fill-the-gap option, predict answer and counterexample must check) before the commit lands. One repair turn is allowed; a valid result is committed as `agent: <summary>` and fast-forwarded with plumbing; an invalid one is discarded.
Why: decision 'Tutor roles: write lessons and exercises'. Lean, not the agent, vouches for what it wrote.
Mirror: ../fret-not/web/server/turn.ts (read its header comment first: when a turn may write, worktree, validation, fast-forward by read-tree and update-ref, cleanup), ../fret-not/web/server/chat.ts, ../fret-not/web/server/tutor-run.test.ts.
Notes: the compile gate runs against the same warm Lean server but in documents of its own. A lesson or concept id that disappears fails validation. Writing is refused (read-only turn, with the reason) unless content/ is exactly the last commit. No hooks, no signing, never `git worktree prune`.
acceptance_criteria:
- A request such as 'write two more exercises on implication' produces one commit touching only content/.
- An exercise whose reference solution fails in Lean never lands; the chat says what failed.
- With uncommitted changes in content/ the turn is read-only and says why.
- Tests cover the gate with a fake agent that writes a good and a bad exercise.

title: Placement check
description:
What: a short check at first run (and on request) that lets the learner skip what he already knows. It samples exercises from each level in order, stops when a level is clearly not yet known, opens the levels passed and credits their concepts, with reviews spread over the following one to two weeks rather than all on one day.
Why: decision 'Progress: placement check'. The learner has symbolic logic training and maths through calculus some time ago, so Level 1 logic may be skipped while the refresher is not.
Mirror: ../fret-not/web/src/pages/Review.tsx (placement), ../fret-not/web/shared/progress.ts (placementConcepts).
Notes: placement is per track where that makes sense (logic can be ahead of the maths refresher). Predict-and-read and fill-the-gap questions make quicker placement items than full proofs.
acceptance_criteria:
- First run offers the check; it can be skipped and retaken.
- Passing levels opens them and credits their concepts with staggered due dates.
- Pure selection and crediting logic is tested.

title: Level unlocks
description:
What: a level opens when the level before it reaches a mastery threshold (Fret Not uses 70% of reviewable concepts), or through the placement check. A level that has opened stays open even if the curriculum later gains a concept. Outlined levels with no exercises ask nothing: the next level looks back past them. Locked levels are visible on the Path with what is needed to open them.
Why: decision 'Progress: levels unlock as mastery builds'.
Mirror: ../fret-not/web/shared/progress.ts (levelStatuses, UNLOCK_FRACTION, openedLevel).
Notes: since there is one adult learner, include a plain 'open anyway' control per level; it is his app.
acceptance_criteria:
- Pure function with tests for: threshold reached, empty level skipped, opened level stays open.
- The Path shows locked, open and done levels.
- 'Open anyway' works and is recorded.

title: Exercise kind: True or false
description:
What: decide whether a claim holds, then back it up. If true, prove it (Lean checks). If false, give a counterexample that Lean checks: the server builds the negated statement and the learner supplies the witness values (and, at higher rungs, the proof that they work). A second form shows a plausible but wrong informal argument and asks which step is flawed (fixed answer, with an explanation).
Why: decisions 'Exercises: all four kinds' and 'Proof craft' (hunting counterexamples is a habit the app teaches).
Where: a new kind in the registry; reuses the Prove it check for both branches.
Notes: choosing the wrong side is itself feedback: trying to prove a false claim should end with 'this cannot be proved; here is why', not an endless attempt. For decidable small cases the checker can close the witness goal with `decide` or `norm_num` so early levels only supply numbers.
acceptance_criteria:
- A true claim is accepted only with a Lean-checked proof; a false one only with a Lean-checked counterexample.
- Picking the wrong side says so and explains.
- The flawed-step form grades against the authored answer and shows its explanation.
- The loader refuses an exercise whose stated truth value has no compiling reference proof or counterexample.

title: Exercise kind: Predict and read
description:
What: three forms. Predict: before a move runs, pick (or type) what the goal becomes; the correct answer is whatever Lean actually returns for that move, computed at load time or on the fly. Match: pair an English statement with its Lean form. Read: given a Lean statement, choose what it claims.
Why: decision 'Exercises: all four kinds'. Builds fluency in reading goal states.
Where: a new kind in the registry. Predict is graded against Lean's real goal state; Match and Read are fixed-answer.
Notes: distractors for Predict are authored in content (common misreadings such as applying the implication the wrong way round). Compare goals after normalising whitespace and hypothesis order. Better with structured goals, but can ship on the text form.
acceptance_criteria:
- All three forms render, grade and record attempts.
- The Predict answer is checked against Lean's goal state, not a string stored by hand; the loader refuses an exercise whose listed correct option disagrees with Lean.
- Tests for grading and for the loader check.

title: Small widgets: truth table, number line, induction dominoes
description:
What: three small lesson widgets. Truth table: build or reveal the table for a propositional formula, with rows the learner can fill in and a note that a truth table checks every case while a proof argues once. Number line: points, intervals and absolute value as distance. Induction dominoes: the base case knocks the first domino, the step case is the rule 'if n falls, n+1 falls'; removing either stops the chain.
Why: the interview said these come along regardless of the four main visuals.
Where: web/src/widgets/, registered in the registry.
Notes: truth table is needed by Level 1, dominoes by Level 2, number line by Level 3.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each is a registered widget with documented parameters and appears in the Gallery.
- The truth table evaluates and, or, not, implies and iff correctly (tested).
- Each is used by at least one lesson when its level is written.
notes: Done in the Level 3 pictures PR: the number line (points, intervals, distance, the window |x - c| < r with a movable x). Remaining: truth table, induction dominoes.

title: Informal beside formal widget
description:
What: a textbook-style proof on the left and the Lean proof on the right, with each sentence linked to the line or lines that formalise it. Hovering or selecting one side highlights the other. The Lean side is real: it is checked by the loader, and its goal state can be shown for the selected line.
Why: decisions 'Visuals: informal beside formal' and 'Proof craft: woven in'. Every lesson shows how a mathematician would say the argument beside the Lean.
Where: a widget in web/src/widgets/; a content format for the pairing (for example numbered sentences in the lesson with a `lines:` reference into a Lean block). Document the format in docs/CONTENT.md.
Notes: the link is many-to-many (one sentence may cover several tactics; 'clearly' in prose may be three Lean lines, which is itself a teaching point).
acceptance_criteria:
- A lesson can declare a paired proof and the widget renders both sides with linked highlighting.
- The loader refuses a pairing whose Lean side does not compile or whose line references are out of range.
- Selecting a Lean line can show the goal state at that line.
- Used in at least the existing If... then lesson.

title: Function and limit explorers
description:
What: interactive graphs for the maths refresher: a function plotter with pan and zoom; an epsilon-delta explorer (drag epsilon, find a delta that works, see the box turn green); secant lines turning into a tangent as h shrinks; Riemann sums with a slider for the number of rectangles; a sequence converging with an epsilon band and the N beyond which every term is inside; inequalities shaded on a number line.
Why: decision 'Visuals: function and limit explorers'. Each idea is shown first, then stated and proved.
Where: web/src/widgets/, registered in the registry, usable in lessons and on the Lab page. Plain SVG or canvas; no charting dependency unless it earns its place. Colours from the tokens in web/src/index.css only.
Notes: functions come from a small safe expression parser (polynomials, rationals, abs, sqrt, sin, cos, exp, log), never `eval`. Level 3 needs the plotter and the number-line inequality view; epsilon-delta, secant, Riemann and sequence views are for Levels 5-6 and the Lab.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each explorer exists as a registered widget with parameters documented in the reference.
- The epsilon-delta explorer reports correctly whether the chosen delta works for the chosen epsilon (tested against known cases).
- Keyboard operable and readable in a narrow window.
- A parser test covers precedence, unary minus, implicit multiplication if supported, and rejection of anything else.
notes: Done in the Level 3 pictures PR: the function plotter (pan, zoom, trace, expression parser with tests) and the number line with shaded intervals. Remaining: epsilon-delta, secant-to-tangent, Riemann sums, sequence convergence.

title: Live proof map
description:
What: a diagram that grows as the learner proves. Hypotheses and intermediate facts are nodes, each move is an arrow from the facts it used to what it produced, open goals are highlighted, a closed goal shows as done, and a move that splits a goal (constructor, cases, induction) draws a branch per new goal. Selecting a node selects the matching Lean line and the reverse.
Why: decision 'Visuals: live proof map'. It shows the shape of an argument and how one move splits or closes goals.
Where: a widget in web/src/widgets/, shown beside the proof board and the typed editor and reused by the Famous Proofs gallery. Build the graph from the goal state before and after each tactic line (one check per prefix of the proof, or one check with a goal query at the end of every line).
Notes: needs the structured goals bead to tell which hypotheses a move consumed and produced. Layout must stay stable as the proof grows: nodes do not jump when a line is added.
acceptance_criteria:
- For 'P → Q, P ⊢ Q' proved by apply then exact, the map shows the two hypotheses, the goal Q, the intermediate goal P and both arrows.
- A constructor on P ∧ Q shows two branches; closing one marks only that branch done.
- Works for clicked and typed proofs, and updates when a line is edited or deleted.
- Clicking a node highlights its Lean line.

title: Ladder fading: the move palette fades into typed Lean
description:
What: the interview chose a ladder: early levels click moves on cards, later levels type freely. Make the rung a property of the exercise (or its level) with at least four steps: (1) full palette, only the moves that are relevant; (2) full palette of every move learned so far; (3) palette hidden behind a 'show moves' control, typing is the default and each palette click only inserts text at the cursor; (4) editor only. The Lean line each click writes is always visible, at every rung.
Why: decision 'Proof input: ladder, visual cards then typed Lean'.
Where: the proof board and typed editor components in web/src/; a `rung` (or similar) field in the lesson's exercise block, with a per-level default in content/curriculum.yaml.
Notes: a learner can always step down a rung for one exercise (a 'show me the moves' control); doing so does not mark the exercise as assisted. Record which rung an attempt was made at.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each rung renders as described and the rung is read from content.
- Level defaults apply when an exercise does not set one.
- The attempt row records the rung.
- Level 1 lessons use rungs 1-2, Level 2 moves to 2-3, Level 3 to 3-4 (set when those levels are written).

title: Structured goals through the Lean RPC interactive-goals API
description:
What: replace the plain-text goal parsing (`$/lean/plainGoal` split on lines) with the language server's RPC session (`$/lean/rpc/connect`, keep-alive, `Lean.Widget.getInteractiveGoals`). Return each goal as data: case name, hypotheses with names, type, optional value, and flags (inserted, removed, instance, inaccessible), and the target, each as tagged text with subexpression positions.
Why: the proof board's cards, the proof map and predict-and-read exercises all need to know exactly which hypothesis is which. Text parsing breaks on multi-line types, grouped binders ('a b : ℕ'), let-values and inaccessible names.
Where: the Lean client in web/server/; the wire types shared with web/src. Keep the plain-text form as a fallback and as the display string.
Notes: the inserted/removed flags give 'what changed after this move' for free; expose them so the board can animate a new card.
acceptance_criteria:
- /api/check returns structured goals for every exercise in content/.
- Hypotheses with multi-line types, grouped binders and let-values are each one card with the right name.
- The diff flags mark hypotheses added and removed by the last move.
- A test pins the structure for at least: an implication, a conjunction split into two goals, and an induction with named cases.

title: Docs, content tooling and README assets
description: File-format contract, generated reference, content checker, data notes, screenshots and the hero image. Source: docs/PRD.md (intake interview, 2026-11-17).

title: Lab and Famous Proofs gallery
description: The open, unscored side of the app. The Playground landed in the first PR; the Lab page and the gallery of classic proofs did not. Source: docs/PRD.md (intake interview, 2026-11-17).

description: Launch from a Dock icon on this Mac, port 38800, like the sibling apps. Source: docs/PRD.md (intake interview, 2026-11-17).

description: The first PR has one Level 1 lesson (If... then). v1 needs Levels 0-3 fully written with Lean-checked exercises, the proof-craft lessons, and outlines for Levels 4-8. Source: docs/PRD.md (intake interview, 2026-11-17).

description: The embedded agent (headless claude -p on the Claude Code login, no API key). The interview chose all four roles. Lean, not the Tutor, always decides whether a proof is correct. Source: docs/PRD.md (intake interview, 2026-11-17).

title: Progress: mastery, spaced review, unlocks, placement
description: The first PR records attempts and exercise and lesson completion. The interview chose Fret Not's model: mastery per concept and tactic, spaced review, level unlocks, placement check. Source: docs/PRD.md (intake interview, 2026-11-17).

title: Exercise kinds beyond Prove it
description: Prove it landed in the first PR. The interview chose four kinds; this epic covers the other three. All are graded by Lean or by fixed answers, never by the Tutor. Source: docs/PRD.md (intake interview, 2026-11-17).

title: Widgets: registry, explorers, informal beside formal, program stepper
description: The visual widgets chosen in the interview, and the registry they hang off. Source: docs/PRD.md (intake interview, 2026-11-17).

title: Proof board: ladder fading and the live proof map
description: The click-to-prove board and typed editor landed in the first PR. This epic covers the ladder from clicking to typing and the proof map. Source: docs/PRD.md (intake interview, 2026-11-17).

title: Lean engine: checker hardening and structured goals
description: The warm lake-serve checker behind /api/check landed in the first PR. This epic covers what makes it trustworthy and richer: axiom checks, timeouts and restart, structured goal data. Source: docs/PRD.md (intake interview, 2026-11-17).

title: Lean checks: cancel a superseded check, and a memory limit
description: What: two things left over from lii-1ou.2. (1) When a typed proof is re-checked on every pause, a check that has been superseded still runs to its end inside Lean before the next starts; cancel it (LSP $/cancelRequest, or skip queued checks of a document when a newer one is waiting). (2) A Lean worker has no memory limit; a proof that allocates without bound is only stopped by the 20 s time limit. Why: both are about one runaway check not slowing the app. Where: web/server/lean/lsp.ts.
notes: From the PR 11 review: identical copies of a timed-out check are already refused with it (lsp.ts doc.timedOut). Still open: queued checks with DIFFERENT text (the learner kept typing) each run to the end or to the limit; all exercises share one document, so one slow check delays every exercise. A file that crashes its worker is deliberately not retried.

title: A calc chain that proves ≤ where < is wanted leaves an unexplained goal like c < c
description: Why: found while fixing the PR #7 review. In math-3-calc/two-links (goal a < c), a chain whose links add up to a ≤ c is not reported as 'this chain proves a ≤ c': Lean extends the chain with a leftover goal 'c < c' (case calc.step), which the typed editor shows as an unfinished proof with nothing said about why. What: recognise the calc.step leftover whose two sides are the same expression and say in plain words that the chain proved a weaker or different relation than the goal. Check the wording against Lean's real message (web/server/lean.test.ts).

title: obtain on a fact that is not an and, or, iff or exists
description:
What: for a fact whose shape shapeOf does not recognise, the board's obtain writes the two-name pattern ⟨h1, h2⟩. Lean refuses most such facts with a message the board explains, but on an equality rcases quietly substitutes it away, and on ∃! the pattern is wrong. Decide per shape: refuse on the board, or write a fitting pattern (unique existence, set membership in an intersection, Even n).
Found by: independent review of PR 4, 2026-11-17. Not reachable in Levels 0-1.
Where: web/shared/moves.ts (obtainLine, misfit).
notes: obtain now handles Even, Odd and divides (hiddenExists in web/shared/moves.ts). Other shapes still fall through to the two-part pattern.

title: Record a board move that changed nothing as an attempt
description:
What: a board move Lean accepts but that leaves the proof state unchanged (norm_num on a goal it cannot touch) is refused in the browser (ProofBoard) and never reaches the attempts table, because the server records a rejected move only when Lean reports an error. Have the client say so (a flag on the check request, or send the previous goals) so the stumble is in the history the Tutor and mastery will read.
Found by: independent reviews of PR 3, 2026-11-17. Judged acceptable to leave for now: it can only withhold a step, never grant one.

title: docs/DATA.md
description:
What: describe what is stored where: the Postgres tables (learner, attempts, completion, later mastery, review, chat, Listen settings), the one implicit learner and how a second would be added, what lives in data/ (Listen cache), setup, migrations, worktree rules (never run db:setup against the real database from a linked worktree), backup and restore.
Mirror: ../fret-not/docs/DATA.md.
Notes: keep it current as the progress, Tutor and Listen beads add tables.
acceptance_criteria:
- docs/DATA.md matches scripts/db/schema.ts table for table.
- Setup, migrate, backup and restore steps are written and tried.

title: Outlines for Levels 4-8 as content
description:
What: turn the outlined levels into content the loader, the Path and the Tutor can use: for each of Level 4 Sets and functions, Level 5 Sequences and limits (epsilon-N), Level 6 Continuity, derivatives, integrals, Level 7 Verified programs: specs, invariants, sort, search (including imperative loops with invariants), Level 8 How large formalisations are built (Mathlib, blueprints, AI provers): concepts with prerequisites in curriculum.yaml, the moves each introduces, a planned lesson list with one-line summaries, and the widgets each needs.
Why: decision 'v1 scope: Levels 4-8 outlined', for the learner and the Tutor to fill in later.
Notes: outlined levels show on the Path as outlined, ask nothing for unlocking, and give the Tutor enough to write a lesson on request.
acceptance_criteria:
- curriculum.yaml carries concepts and planned lessons for Levels 4-8 and loads cleanly.
- The Path shows each as outlined with its summary.
- docs/PRD.md's Curriculum section and curriculum.yaml agree.

title: Tutor research maps for current results
description:
What: given a result in the news (an AI-assisted proof, a newly formalised theorem), the Tutor searches the web and builds a plain-language map: what was claimed, by whom and when; what was formally verified and in which system, as distinct from what was announced or argued informally; which concepts in the path it rests on, linked to their lessons; and what is still open or disputed. Maps are saved (a 'Field notes' section) with their sources and the date they were made.
Why: decision 'Tutor roles: explain current research results'.
Where: a Tutor mode with web search allowed; saved maps live in Postgres or under data/, not in content/.
Notes: needs internet. Every claim in a map carries a source link; a map must say plainly when it could not confirm something. The app ships no built-in claims about any specific recent result.
acceptance_criteria:
- Asking about a named result yields a map with the four parts above and working source links.
- 'Claimed' and 'formally verified' are separate sections and the distinction is explicit.
- Maps are saved, dated and reopenable; offline, the feature says it needs internet.
- Concept links resolve to lessons in the path (or say 'outlined, not yet written').

title: Database backup script
description:
What: `npm run db:backup` writes a timestamped pg_dump of the lean_into_it database to a gitignored backups/ folder and prunes old ones; optionally a launchd plist to run it daily.
Why: progress and attempt history exist only in local Postgres.
Mirror: ../lingo-dojo/scripts/db/backup-cli.mjs and the db:backup and db:backup:plist scripts in ../lingo-dojo/package.json.
Notes: add backups/ to .gitignore. Refuse to run from a linked worktree without its own DATABASE_URL, as the sibling setup scripts do.
acceptance_criteria:
- npm run db:backup produces a restorable dump and prunes beyond the keep count.
- Restore steps are written in docs/DATA.md.
- A test covers naming and pruning without a real server.

title: Program stepper
description:
What: step through a small Lean function's evaluation with the state shown at each step: the call being reduced, the arguments, the result so far. Recursion is drawn as a tree that mirrors the induction proof (base case leaf, step case node), and a stated property is checked at each step and shown holding.
Why: decision 'Visuals: program stepper', for the verified-programs track (functional first, loops later).
Where: a widget in web/src/widgets/. For v1 the functions are recursive functions on Nat, List and trees; the trace can come from Lean itself (instrumented evaluation via #eval of a tracing version) or from a small evaluator for the subset of Lean used in lessons. Choose in the bead and record why.
Notes: imperative loops with invariants are an outlined later level (Level 7); design the trace format so a loop's state and invariant can be added without rework.
acceptance_criteria:
- Stepping forward and back through length, append and reverse on a short list shows the right call tree and values.
- The tree for a structural recursion visibly matches the cases of the induction proof shown beside it.
- A property (for example length (xs ++ ys) = length xs + length ys) is evaluated at each node.
- Registered in the registry and shown in the Gallery.
